rule: Four hand-scored places per class and band, taken from app_data/curated_appeal.json, whose hand appeal sits in the band and whose why fits its test. A rubric score is placed against the anchors of its own class: first the band whose test fits, then the position inside the band. appeal is the hand scale (0 to 10, before appeal_scale.py), the same scale the rubric writes.
shortfalls: city Exceptional: 2 anchors (only Venice and Bruges are hand-scored 9.0 or more among rated city rows)
town Exceptional: 2 anchors (only Pompeii and Dubrovnik)
village Exceptional: the only 4 hand scores at 9.0 or more; Meteora and Sognefjord are landscapes filed as villages by population

calibration_about: T758: 30 well-known hand-scored places in the Good and Pleasant range, two per class and range, the most visited first. Added after the first three shards scored their hidden controls 0.4 to 1.4 above the hand scale: the hand scale is strict for famous places that are pleasant rather than compelling. Not anchors, not controls, not in the blind hand check.
